references.text: The original instruction from God on how the cherubim were to be made, with wings spread upward and faces turned toward each other and toward the mercy seat.
The entire description of the mercy seat with the cherubim that God gave to Moses on the mountain, which Bezalel now carries out in Exodus 37.
Solomon made cherubim for the temple that also had outstretched wings, and the wings touched each other.
The cherubim in Solomon's temple spread their wings over the ark of the covenant and the mercy seat.
Chronicles' description of the cherubim in Solomon's temple with outstretched wings.
Ezekiel's vision of the cherubim with outstretched wings above their heads.
Ezekiel's vision of the cherubim at God's throne with their wings.
The Hebrews mentions the glorious cherubim who overshadowed the mercy seat, a direct reference to these cherubim.
Describes the historical fulfillment of the pattern in Solomon's temple, where the cherubim cover the ark.
Confirms through Solomon's account that the cherubim covered the ark as planned.
Expands the understanding of the cherubim's position from covering the ark to filling the entire holy place.
Provides an interesting theological contrast point in that the cherubim in the temple face toward the house, not down toward the ark.
